submitted.rationale: Index 16 (Sb 0.68, near trirutile ZnSb2O6) had the highest EQE of the three measurements: 0.0069%, versus about 0.0029% at both ends of the composition line. All values are very low, which fits wide-gap Sb(V)–Zn oxides responding only weakly to 2.7 eV light.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0029%, the Zn-rich spinel Zn7Sb2O12 region
Measured EQE 0.0029%, the Sb-rich region; the hoped-for visible absorption from Sb mixed-valence oxides did not appear

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE predicts ~1.97 eV for trirutile ZnSb2O6 (mp-3188) and ~1.95 eV for spinel Zn7Sb2O12, vs 4.2 eV for Sb(III) ZnSb2O4. Both Sb(V) phases would absorb 2.7 eV photons if these predictions hold (experimental gaps are nearer 3.3 eV, so I only partly trust this). Weak support for measuring index 16 (Sb 0.68), which sits near the ZnSb2O6 stoichiometry.

MACE puts spinel Zn7Sb2O12 (mp-675797) almost on the hull (0.012 eV/atom), so index 0 (Sb 0.226, matching the 0.222 stoichiometry) should form this phase cleanly. Its predicted gap of ~1.95 eV means 2.7 eV light can be absorbed. Index 16 near ZnSb2O6 gave very low EQE, so I'm checking the opposite end of the line. Support.

MEGNet puts mixed-valence Sb6O13 at ~2.05 eV (HSE), below 2.7 eV. So Sb-rich compositions that mix ZnSb2O6 with an Sb-oxide phase could absorb more visible light. EQE so far rises with Sb (0.0029% at Sb 0.23, 0.0069% at Sb 0.68), and the GP suggests the 20–22 region. Moderate support for index 22 (Sb 0.80).
